text:
Gray and quiet to start this Tuesday, 43 now, and the morning should stay mostly dry. Showers move in this afternoon, mainly from about 4 until 7 or so, and they're light, under a tenth of an inch. One model is a lot wetter than the others, so I'd stick the umbrella in the bag anyway. The high is 51, then it's cloudy and about 39 tonight, with the last of the showers done by bedtime.

Veterans Day looks mostly cloudy, chilly and mostly dry, with a high near 48. A jacket day, but no rain gear needed.

The bigger story is Thursday. A stronger system arrives with rain, and highs hold in the low 40s. The forecasters say it's too mild here for snow to be a worry in town. Any accumulating snow stays up high, though it could creep lower Thursday night into Friday as colder air wraps in behind it. That timing is still unsettled, so check back Wednesday. Plan on a wet, raw Thursday.

week.blurb: Showers arrive mid-morning and fade by tonight, with under a tenth of an inch and a high near 51, so keep the umbrella handy.
Veterans Day stays dry and mostly cloudy, a touch cooler with a high near 48 and a chilly evening around 35.
Clouds hold and a rain and snow mix is possible from the morning on, with a high near 46 and no accumulation expected.
Looks like a raw, gray Friday with a few early flakes, then a rain and snow mix possible, and a high near 42.
Trending cloudy and cold with a high near 43, and a mix of rain and snow possible at times, nothing steady.
If the pattern holds, a leftover rain and snow mix fades by early afternoon, leaving a mostly cloudy day with a high near 45.
Looks like a drier start to the week, with partly sunny skies and a high near 46.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A strong synoptic scale system is expected to produce a widespread precip event acrs our cwa Thursday into Friday with some wet snow possible over the higher terrain, but potential hazards/impacts still to be determined. 00z guidance, including the GFS ensemble and associated AI-GFS prog a deepening and closing off full latitude trof over the Mid Atlantic/NE CONUS late Thurs into Friday. The primary issue for snow lovers like myself is the lack of cold air initially, especially with no arctic or modified arctic high pres located to our north/northeast. So we are going to need very high precip rates to help bring slightly cooler air toward the sfc and elevation to see accumulating snowfall, especially with bl temps btwn 2-3C per latest GFS sounding data at BTV. Sounding data indicates very marginal thermal profiles, especially on Thursday with progged 850mb temps hovering near 0C and 925mb 0 to 1C, which supports snow levels above 3000 feet and minimal impacts. However, as system pulls away, winds shift to the northwest and llvl caa develops on backside, allowing thermal profiles to cool and support some accumulating snowfall. The challenge is how quickly does the cooler air advect on backside and does moisture linger around to support accumulation snowfall. At this time, the highest probability (60-80%) of several inches of accumulating snowfall would be acrs the Dacks and Green mtns of VT, Thurs night thru Friday. GFS is very slow with lifting mid/upper lvl circulation eastward with sfc weakness/invert trof lingering into Saturday. This idea would support additional snowfall possible, especially trrn. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -We are stuck in a very November-like pattern with clouds and mixed showers. Tuesday looks to start mainly dry, but showers start to make their return into Tuesday afternoon and evening, especially the further north you are. Some sunshine could emerge off to the south. Temperatures are in the 40s to lower 50s for Tuesday afternoon. Clouds remain stubborn all the way through midweek with mostly cloudy skies overhead for both Wednesday and Thursday. Temperatures start to turn a bit cooler, as they fall into the mid and upper 40s for Wednesday and the low to mid 40s for Thursday. Rain and higher elevation snow showers develop Thursday, especially by afternoon, as an area of low pressure approaches. Right now there is a question of how much of this can become accumulating snow outside of the mountains. We do turn drier into early next week, with mainly cloudy skies by Sunday and a few breaks of sunshine possible for Monday. Temperatures start to rebound a bit back into the low to mid 40s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-09T22:30:00Z — same caveat): Cloudy with additional showers Tuesday, brighter south — Tonight turns drier, with only a lingering sprinkle or flurry. Expect a mostly cloudy sky, with lows in the 30s to around 40. After a dry start to Tuesday, another round of scattered showers comes through by afternoon and evening, especially in northern areas. A few embedded downpours are possible. Highs reach the low 50s. More breaks of sun are likely in southern Vermont. Wednesday (Veterans Day) looks mostly dry, with only a spot shower or flurry possible. However, it will be mostly cloudy and chilly, with highs in the upper 40s. The late-week stretch looks quite chilly, as the jet stream dips farther south. Highs only reach the low to mid-40s, with lots of clouds. Rain and elevation snow showers develop Thursday, especially by afternoon, as an area of low pressure approaches. Depending on the storm track, a period of steadier rain and mountain snow is possible Friday, with mixed showers lingering into Saturday. Drier weather is likely early next week, followed by a warmup into the 50s.
